title: Taking an external file into the graph
summary: A file read in the browser, parsed and duplicate-checked into a staging batch, reviewed row by row by a person, and only then committed — with rollback still available afterwards.
note: Nothing reaches the graph without an explicit commit: staging writes only to imports, import_rows and import_raw_chunks. Files are never uploaded as multipart — the browser reads them with FileReader and posts the text as JSON, which is why app.ts:51 mounts a 15 MB parser for this prefix ahead of the 2 MB default. Duplicate detection runs once, at staging time, against the graph as it was then; it is not re-run at commit, so a long review can go stale. The GitHub sync route (routes/v1/imports.ts:60) is a different shape entirely — it writes directly with no staging — and is not drawn here.

actors.label: Person (Import hub)
actors.note: Reads the file locally with FileReader and posts its text. Reviews every staged row before anything is committed.

actors.label: imports router
actors.note: Zod-validates kind and content; maps a parse failure to 422 INVALID_IMPORT_CONTENT rather than a 500.

actors.label: @vitae/core importers
actors.note: Pure parsers per format: LinkedIn archives, vCard, iCalendar, mapped CSV, Netscape bookmarks, résumé text, Aperture bundles.

actors.label: @vitae/core dedup
actors.note: comparePersons/scorePair and the generic compareEntities. Returns non_match, possible or probable with weighted evidence.

actors.label: Postgres
actors.note: Staging lives in imports / import_rows / import_raw_chunks; the commit writes nodes, edges, atoms, variants, taggings and revisions.

actors.label: Search index
actors.note: Marked dirty after a commit or rollback; the duplicate scan cache is invalidated too so the identity audit does not serve a pre-import queue.

steps.label: POST /api/v1/imports { kind, filename, content, mapping? }
steps.note: The file is text in a JSON body, not multipart. A connections export runs to several megabytes, which is what the prefix-scoped parser exists for.

steps.label: 422 VALIDATION (kind/content) or 422 INVALID_IMPORT_CONTENT (unparseable)
steps.note: 413 PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE comes earlier still, from the body parser, mapped explicitly so an oversized file does not read as 'something went wrong'.

steps.label: parse the content into rows (and, for a bundle, its edges)
steps.note: A LinkedIn archive is sniffed by header to tell positions, education, skills and connections apart. Résumé text is disassembled into candidate atom lines: bullets and substantial sentences.

steps.label: load the whole graph once, indexed by type and by identity key
steps.note: One load serves every row's duplicate check. Person rows additionally get the organisation names each existing person is linked to, so a shared employer can count as evidence.

steps.label: per row: score against existing candidates of the same type
steps.note: A bundle row with a matching external identity key short-circuits to 'probable' before any scoring. Otherwise people go through weighted field comparison (email, phone, name trigram, shared org domain), and other types hit bespoke rules first — exact URL for links, title and date for events, normalised name for skills and education, title and company for roles — falling back to the generic entity comparison only when none of those fire. Atom rows are never duplicate-checked at all.

steps.label: verdict + weight + human-readable evidence, or nothing
steps.note: The best-scoring candidate wins; non_match candidates are discarded. Evidence is rendered as phrases like 'email match' or 'name similar' so the reviewer sees why, not just that.

steps.label: write the batch, the raw upload in chunks, and every staged row
steps.note: A 'probable' duplicate defaults the row to skip and everything else to accept (services/imports.ts:589). That default is the only thing the machine decides — it is a proposal, and it is reversible in the next step.

steps.label: 201 { batch, rows } — nothing has touched the graph
PATCH /imports/:id/rows/:rowId { decision, payload? }
steps.note: This is the confirmation step. A reviewer flips accept/skip per row and may patch the payload — which is also how an unassigned résumé line gets an owner before it can become an atom.

steps.label: POST /imports/:id/discard — abandon the batch
steps.note: Discarding is a deletion intent: discardImport (services/imports.ts:1104) purges the raw upload — address book, calendar, resume text — with the batch. FR-006: nothing survives a discard.

steps.label: per accepted row: create the node, its edges, or the atom + variant + revision
steps.note: Deterministic ids: a row with an external identity key hashes to a stable node id, so re-importing the same record updates nothing rather than duplicating. Skipped rows create nothing at all.

steps.label: a row that throws is recorded as failed and stays staged
steps.note: One malformed row never aborts the batch. Failed rows keep their reason, the batch stays 'staged' so it can be fixed and re-committed, and only a clean run closes it and purges the raw upload (services/imports.ts:1085).

steps.label: mark the index dirty and invalidate the duplicate scan
{ created, failed } — and POST /imports/:id/rollback is still available
steps.note: Rollback (routes/v1/imports.ts:110) soft-deletes every node, edge and atom the batch created and purges the raw upload, so a committed batch is not a one-way door.
